 Rivian (RIVN) Stock May Be 32% Undervalued As R2 Hopes Grow
 November 8, 2026, 21:17 UTC SA Sasha Jovanovic Rivian Automotive has seen its share price move sharply over the past few years, and the latest bounce has renewed a simple question for investors. Is the current US$13.61 price actually supported by the cash the business is expected to generate over time, or is the recent optimism running ahead of those cash flows?
 Over the past 5 years the stock has fallen 89.5%. That puts the spotlight firmly on whether the current valuation still lines up with the long term cash generation story.
 Recent upgrades from large banks that point to future production of the R2 line and a path toward positive automotive gross profit suggest that investors are now treating future margins and the timing of cash inflows as key drivers of what the shares might be worth today.
 If you'd rather focus on sales, this one's for you. See why Rivian Automotive's 3.1x P/S tells a different valuation story .
 The stock's next move may depend on whether the intrinsic value estimate from the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model supports or challenges the price implied by Rivian Automotive's current share level.
 If you want to stress test this same cash flow question beyond Rivian Automotive, explore a wider field of electric and future-focused auto players using our screener containing 19 high quality undiscovered gems 
 Advertisement Does Rivian Automotive Look Undervalued on Cash Flow?
 The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model values Rivian Automotive based on the cash it could generate for shareholders over time. The latest twelve month free cash flow shows an outflow of about US$4.3b, and analyst projections still have Rivian using cash for several more years before moving to positive free cash flow around 2030, followed by subsequent growth.
 Those cash flow forecasts imply recovering and then expanding economics, which results in a DCF estimate that is substantially above the current US$13.61 share price. UBS highlighting R2 production and a path to positive automotive gross profit helps explain why the cash flow curve in the model improves over time, even if the current price still reflects the heavy spending phase more than the later cash generation.  Rivian Automotive splits opinion, with some community members seeing extra upside and others focusing on execution and funding strain.
 Bull case: 25% undervalued 
 "The main thing that has to go right is that Rivian converts its software-defined vehicle and autonomy stack, along with partnerships such as Volkswagen and Uber, into durable software and licensing revenue streams…" Discover why this Narrative puts Rivian Automotive at 25% undervalued .
 Bear case: roughly fairly valued 
 "Even with over US$14b of existing and targeted liquidity from cash, public equity, loans, and partner funding, the combination of multi year capital expenditure for R2, the Georgia plant, autonomy hardware, and robotaxi commitments means Rivian Automotive could still need additional external capital if execution slips…" Explore why this Narrative puts Rivian Automotive at roughly fairly valued .

A group of US manufacturers including First Solar, Qcells and Suniva accuses TOYO of routing Chinese parts through Ethiopia to dodge US duties on Chinese solar products. Commerce expects a preliminary decision on 10 December 2026 and a final one around 10 May 2027. If it goes against TOYO, duties can be collected on shipments back to the inquiry's start on 17 July. That hits TOYO's core: 4 GW of cell capacity in Hawassa, Ethiopia, with 80.7% of H1 revenue coming from US customers. TOYO denies the claim.New tariffs from 4 December. Imported cells will face a 15% duty plus a minimum price of $0.22 per watt. Management is negotiating a framework with Commerce. The rules let companies with approved US investment plans import some volume without the duty, and that exemption is TOYO's hope.
